articles.title: Rochdale AFC launches Christmas Toy Appeal for local families in need
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC is calling on fans to donate gifts for its Christmas Toy Appeal, aiming to support local children living in poverty this festive season.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC has launched its Christmas Toy Appeal, urging fans to donate presents for local families in need this festive season.

The initiative aims to support children living in poverty across the borough, with donations being collected at the Family Stand of the Crown Oil Arena.

Last year, the club received an impressive 455 gifts from supporters, and this year, they hope to surpass that total. The donated presents will be distributed to local children, ensuring they have something special to open on Christmas Day.

The appeal is a long-standing partnership between Rochdale AFC and the community, highlighting the club's commitment to helping those less fortunate during the holiday season. Fans are encouraged to contribute to this worthy cause and make a difference in the lives of struggling families.

The Christmas Toy Appeal not only aims to provide joy to children but also fosters community spirit and involvement.

Donations can be made at the Crown Oil Arena, and the club is calling on the generosity of its supporters to help make this Christmas special for local families.
articles.social_headline: Rochdale AFC asks fans to donate toys for local families this Christmas

articles.title: Boy, 3, dies after Middleton nursery incident as police open investigation
articles.excerpt: GMP says the boy died on 5 November after emergency services were called to Cosy Toes Nursery on 2 November. No arrests have been made.
articles.content_html:
A three-year-old boy has died after an emergency at a Middleton nursery, and police have opened an investigation into the circumstances.

Greater Manchester Police said on Wednesday 18 November that the boy died in hospital on Thursday 5 November. Emergency services had been called to Cosy Toes Nursery on Mainway East shortly before 4pm on Monday 2 November following a report of concern for a child.

Officers attended alongside other emergency services and the boy was taken to hospital. His family is being supported by specialist officers.

GMP said an investigation had been opened in line with usual procedure because the circumstances leading up to his death occurred in a care setting. No arrests have been made.

Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan said: "This is an incredibly tragic development in a deeply upsetting incident and our thoughts remain with the boy's family."

She added: "We are in the very early stages of our involvement and are carefully considering events and the evidence available to us. For now, we ask that the family's privacy is respected as they begin to navigate the unimaginable loss of their little boy."

The police statement gives no cause of death and makes no allegation of wrongdoing against any named person or organisation.

Anyone with information that could help the investigation can report it online to Greater Manchester Police or call 0161 856 3635. Information can also be given anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or through its website.

Update, 18 November 2026: This article previously reported that the boy was in a critical condition. It has been updated following GMP's confirmation of his death and the opening of an investigation.

articles.title: Bev Craig criticises plans for Seven Sisters demolition in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig has expressed disappointment over the decision to demolish the Seven Sisters tower blocks, highlighting ongoing issues with the housing provider.
articles.content_html:
Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig has expressed disappointment over Rochdale Boroughwide Housing's (RBH) decision to demolish the Seven Sisters tower blocks, which will see 766 flats replaced with 601 new homes.

The announcement was made on 16 November 2026, marking a significant change for the College Bank site that has been under scrutiny for a decade.

The demolition plan has been met with mixed reactions, particularly from the approximately 80 households still residing in the Seven Sisters. Many tenants have already left due to the uncertainty surrounding the future of the site, which has been earmarked for demolition since 2016.

Campaigners advocating for the refurbishment of the 1960s blocks have expressed their concerns over the loss of existing homes.

In a recent interview on BBC Radio Manchester, Ms Craig stated that the decision to proceed with demolition without a clear timeline for replacement homes is 'incredibly disappointing'.

She highlighted ongoing issues with the housing provider, RBH, and noted that the situation has been '10 years in the making'.

The Seven Sisters towers have been a contentious issue in Rochdale, with community advocates pushing for alternatives to demolition.

The latest announcement brings an end to years of uncertainty for residents and campaigners alike, as the focus now shifts to the development of new housing on the site.

articles.title: St Cuthbert’s RC High School in Rochdale placed in special measures after Ofsted inspection
articles.excerpt: St Cuthbert’s RC High School in Rochdale has been placed in special measures following an Ofsted inspection that highlighted serious safety issues and a lack of effective leadership.
articles.content_html:
St Cuthbert’s RC High School in Rochdale has been placed in special measures after an Ofsted inspection on 6 October revealed that pupils do not feel safe and that harmful behaviours have become normalised.

The inspection report indicated that the school is failing to provide an acceptable standard of education and lacks the necessary leadership to secure improvements.

Inspectors noted significant concerns regarding safeguarding standards, stating that leaders have not ensured a positive culture around safeguarding to protect pupils from harm.

This situation follows a period of industrial action by staff, who protested against safety concerns between February and June 2026, in a dispute with the St Teresa of Calcutta Catholic Academy Trust, which oversees the school.

Ofsted's Chief Inspector noted that the governing body has been disbanded and replaced by a trust intervention committee, with an interim executive headteacher appointed since November 2025.

The urgent need for improvement at St Cuthbert’s RC High School raises significant concerns for the local community, particularly for parents and students.

The school will now be under close scrutiny as it attempts to address the issues identified by Ofsted and restore a safe learning environment for its pupils.

articles.title: Life Without Limits gym relocates to new premises in Littleborough
articles.excerpt: Life Without Limits fitness centre has received planning permission to move to a larger facility on Stockton Street, allowing for expansion and new services.
articles.content_html:
Life Without Limits fitness centre has been granted permission to relocate to a new site at 3a and 3b Stockton Street, Littleborough, as it continues to expand its services.

The gym, which currently operates from Unit 12a on the Paragon Industrial Estate, will move to a larger facility that will allow it to consolidate and expand its offerings, including group exercise, personal training, physiotherapy, and wellbeing services.

Joshua Smith, the applicant, noted in the planning documents that the business has grown significantly since its establishment and currently employs around 12 staff members. The new premises could potentially double the workforce as the business develops further.

This relocation is part of a broader trend of growth for the independent gym, which aims to better serve the community's fitness needs and enhance its service offerings.

evidence_sources.captured_text: New home will help independent gym grow - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS New home will help independent gym grow A gym and fitness centre has been given permission to relocate as it continues to expand. Joshua Smith applied to Rochdale Council for change of use permission to turn an industrial unit into a gymnasium at 3a and 3b Stockton Street, Littleborough. The change will enable the independent Life Without Limits fitness centre to relocate from its current base at Unit 12a on the Paragon Industrial Estate. Planning documents submitted with the application state: “The business currently provides gym and fitness facilities alongside group exercise, personal training, children’s fitness, physiotherapy, rehabilitation, Pilates, recovery and wellbeing services. “The business has developed significantly since its establishment and currently employs and works alongside approximately 12 staff members and health and fitness professionals providing a wide range of services and facilities. “The proposed premises would allow the business to consolidate and expand these activities within a larger facility. “The proposal is being brought forward in response to the established growth of an existing local business and its requirement for premises capable of supporting its next stage of development. “The applicant anticipates that the expanded operation could at least double the existing workforce and professional team as the business develops. READ MORE: Teenager tackles adversity to keep rugby dreams alive “The proposed use would therefore continue and increase the employment function of the premises while simply changing the nature of the employment generated.” The plans do not include any external alterations to the site, which has been recently renovated. A planning officer’s report said: “The relocation of the gym would see the business occupy a larger unit with increase in size footprint required to help support the local business grow. “The proposed change of use from general industrial use to a new gym, would also allow for a vacant unit to be returned to use. “It is also noted that the existing industrial estate appears to be underutilised with a number of empty/unoccupied units. Additionally, as noted in the supporting report, the business presently has approximately 12 staff with additional health and fitness professionals. “Relocation to a larger site would likely see the number of employees and other professionals who use the gym increase. “Although gyms are considered to be main town centre uses, noting the proposed use of the site, it is considered that the proposal would be of an appropriate scale and character to the area and would not be detrimental to the businesses within the industrial estate.” Granting permission, the council set opening hours from 6am to 10pm Monday to Friday and 8am to 8pm on Saturdays and Sundays. articles.title: Rochdale house prices rise by 4.1% over the past year
articles.excerpt: House prices in Rochdale have increased by 4.1% over the past year, with the average home now costing £213,000, according to the latest data from the Office for National Statistics.
articles.content_html:
House prices in Rochdale have increased by 4.1% over the past year, with the average home now costing £213,000, according to the latest data from the Office for National Statistics.

This rise reflects a steady demand for housing in the area, despite broader trends across Greater Manchester.

In comparison, Stockport has emerged as a property hotspot, with average prices climbing by 5.2% to £322,000, making it the borough with the highest growth in the region. Trafford follows closely, with an average home price of £394,000, reflecting a 4.7% increase.

Other boroughs such as Wigan and Bury also reported increases of 4.0% and 3.3%, respectively, indicating a general upward trend in property values across most of Greater Manchester.

Salford is the only borough in Greater Manchester to experience a decline in house prices, with a decrease of 1.6%, bringing the average home price down to £226,000.

The increase in house prices in Rochdale may impact local residents looking to buy homes, as affordability becomes a growing concern. Potential buyers and sellers will need to consider these trends when making decisions regarding property transactions.

articles.title: Rochdale restaurant's Sunday roast named among the best in the UK
articles.excerpt: The Martlet in Rochdale has been recognised for its exceptional Sunday roast in a national ranking by the Good Food Guide.
articles.content_html:
A restaurant in Rochdale has been recognised for serving one of the best Sunday roasts in the UK.

The Martlet, located in Rochdale town centre, was featured in the Good Food Guide's list of the top 40 roasts across the country, highlighting its commitment to quality and local produce.

The Martlet opened in September 2024 inside the historic Rochdale Town Hall, which recently underwent extensive refurbishments. The Good Food Guide praised the restaurant for its 'sturdy simplicity' and its focus on traditional dishes made with local ingredients.

The review noted the restaurant's unique setting within the Victorian Gothic architecture of the town hall.

Among the standout menu items are the 'sell-out' pies and a selection of culturally diverse dishes, including coriander bhajis and rigatoni with meatballs.

The roast dinners, featuring options like roast sirloin of Cheshire beef and garlicky, minty leg of Dales lamb, were described as equally traditional and well-prepared, complete with all the trimmings.

The recognition of the Martlet not only enhances its reputation but also contributes positively to Rochdale's culinary scene, attracting both locals and visitors to experience the acclaimed Sunday roast.
articles.social_headline: Rochdale's Martlet restaurant serves one of the best Sunday roasts in the UK

articles.title: Rochdale's Springhill Hospice wins three garden awards
articles.excerpt: An 18-strong volunteer gardening team has helped Springhill Hospice win three awards, including Best Hospice Garden in the North West 2026.
articles.content_html:
Springhill Hospice's volunteer gardeners have been recognised with three awards, including Best Hospice Garden in the North West 2026.

The Rochdale hospice says the honours recognise the work of its 18 volunteer gardeners, who look after the grounds throughout the year, alongside support from local residents and businesses.

As well as the regional title at the North West in Bloom Awards, Springhill received Level 5 Outstanding in the Rochdale in Bloom: It's Your Neighbourhood Awards. That is the highest level of recognition in the scheme.

A separate Level 5 Outstanding Five Year Achievement Award recognised the consistently high standard of the gardens during the five years the hospice has entered.

Head gardener Claire Connely said: “Week after week, come rain or shine, our volunteers give their time, skills and energy to care for the gardens and create something truly special for everyone who visits Springhill.”

The gardens give patients and their families somewhere to sit together, enjoy the changing seasons and find a quiet moment. For a charity supporting adults with life-limiting conditions across Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale, the grounds are part of the space shared by patients, loved ones, staff and volunteers.

The hospice said its Business Buddies and corporate volunteers also contribute time, expertise and practical help. Residents and organisations donate plants, pots, coffee grounds and gardening materials.

Among the regular supporters is the team at 3 Pitts allotment, which grows and donates 400 begonias each spring for planting around the hospice grounds.

Claire said: “Our gardens really are a community effort. We are incredibly fortunate to have so many people and local businesses who support us, whether that's giving their time, sharing their expertise or donating something we can put to good use.”

The three awards recognise both the garden team's year-round work and the wider community support behind the grounds.

Source: Springhill Hospice press release supplied on 18 November 2026.

articles.title: Healey Dell tearooms win North West in Bloom gold for fifth year running
articles.excerpt: Healey Dell Heritage Centre and Tearooms has won North West in Bloom gold for a fifth year, and this year also took home a trophy.
articles.content_html:
Healey Dell Heritage Centre and Tearooms, tucked between Rochdale and Whitworth, has won a North West in Bloom Gold Award for the fifth year running.

This year the centre also came home with a trophy, presented by local councillors.

The glass trophy, from Britain in Bloom with the RHS, North West, is inscribed "For Best Small Tourist Attraction".

According to the centre, if it wins again next year it gets to keep the trophy.

In a post announcing the win, the centre said it was "immensely proud of what has been achieved here at Healey Dell".

It thanked its visitors, customers and friends for their support, and most of all its staff and volunteers.

"Their hard work and dedication are a huge part of why this wonderful little place continues to receive recognition," the centre said.

It added: "Five years of Gold and now a Trophy. Not bad for a tearoom tucked away in our beautiful little corner between Rochdale and Whitworth!"

The centre has invited people to visit for a cuppa and a bite to eat.

Source: Healey Dell Heritage Centre and Tearooms, supplied to Rochdale Daily. Photograph: Healey Dell Heritage Centre and Tearooms.

articles.title: Rochdale MP seeks local role in pilot targeting repeat shoplifters
articles.excerpt: Greater Manchester has been selected for a programme targeting repeat shop theft, but the locations have yet to be decided. Paul Waugh wants Rochdale included.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale's town and district centres should be included in a new programme targeting repeat shoplifters, the town's MP has said, after Greater Manchester was selected to take part.

Paul Waugh's office said Policing and Crime Minister Sarah Jones had confirmed the force area's place in the Prolific Retail Offenders Pilot Programme in a letter this week. Local delivery plans are still being drawn up, and Rochdale has not yet been confirmed as a focus for the scheme.

The programme will bring police, probation, councils, housing and treatment services together with retailers to concentrate on people responsible for repeated shop theft. Alongside enforcement, it aims to address problems such as drug and alcohol misuse and unstable housing that can contribute to persistent offending.

Decisions about where work will be concentrated within Greater Manchester will be made locally, based on patterns of offending, according to the MP's office. No Rochdale start date, allocation of funding or number of people to be targeted was given in the release.

Mr Waugh said: "Shopkeepers and their staff in Rochdale tell me time and again that it is often the same faces coming back, week after week."

He said he would press local police and partners to include Rochdale's high streets and speak to retailers and business groups about their experience of repeat offending.

The Home Office's national announcement on 18 November said the programme would target around 500 prolific retail offenders across up to 16 police forces, with an initial £2.5 million available for participating forces and partners overall. That is a national funding pot, rather than an announced sum for Rochdale.

The National Police Chiefs' Council said the pilot would test a more intensive approach involving several agencies, with the aim of reducing repeat offending and improving outcomes for retailers and communities.

For Rochdale shop staff and businesses, the next decision is whether local centres are chosen for delivery. The MP's office has invited businesses to share their experiences with it.

Source: Office of Paul Waugh MP, press release issued on 18 November 2026; Home Office; National Police Chiefs' Council. Image: Rochdale Daily file photograph of police.

articles.title: Rochdale Metrolink patrols target knife crime during Sceptre week
articles.excerpt: Town centre PCSOs have patrolled the tram route between Newbold and Rochdale town centre as part of the national knife crime campaign.
articles.content_html:
Police community support officers have carried out patrols on the Metrolink between Newbold and Rochdale town centre as part of a national campaign against knife crime.

PCSO Tyler Davies, from Rochdale Town Centre’s neighbourhood team, confirmed the activity in a police community alert published on Tuesday 17 November. The patrols form part of Operation Sceptre, which combines enforcement, prevention and community engagement.

The local alert reports the patrols but gives no figures for arrests or weapons recovered.

In a separate statement issued on Wednesday 18 November, Greater Manchester Police outlined plans for the national week of action. Across the force, these include weapons searches, visible patrols, targeted enforcement, test purchases in shops and sessions with schools and communities.

GMP said its school engagement officers work with schools across Greater Manchester on knife crime prevention, including support for teachers through the Pol-Ed education platform.

Detective Superintendent Richard Thompson, who leads the force’s response to knife crime and serious violence, said: "Whilst the progress we have seen in reducing knife-enabled robberies is positive, we are not complacent."

He said the campaign combines action against people carrying and using weapons with education and prevention. The force’s work continues throughout the year.

GMP also held an online question and answer session on Monday 16 November, covering topics including safe knife disposal and support for young people. The questions and answers remain available at https://app.sli.do/event/mPTtysYyVsSfUCZKNaxEmE/live/questions.

Sources: Rochdale Town Centre PCSO Tyler Davies’s Operation Sceptre alert, published 17 November 2026, https://neighbourhoodalert.co.uk/Alerts/A/527035/Op-Sceptre; GMP Press Office statement, 18 November 2026, https://www.gmp.police.uk/news/greater-manchester/news/news/2026/november/knife-enabled-robberies-continue-to-fall-as-gmp-launch-national-week-of-action-tackling-knife-crime-and-protecting-communities/.

articles.title: Investigation launched after death of three-year-old boy at Middleton nursery
articles.excerpt: A three-year-old boy has died following an incident at Cosy Toes Nursery in Middleton, prompting a police investigation and the nursery's closure.
articles.content_html:
A three-year-old boy has died following an incident at Cosy Toes Nursery on Mainway East in Middleton on 2 November. Emergency services were called to the nursery, and the boy was transported to hospital, where he sadly passed away three days later.

In response to the incident, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) have launched an investigation, stating that no arrests have been made at this stage.

Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan described the situation as "incredibly tragic" and emphasized the need for privacy for the boy's family during this difficult time.

Cosy Toes Nursery has been closed for six weeks following the incident, with Ofsted suspending its registration. An Ofsted spokesperson expressed condolences to the family and confirmed their cooperation with the police investigation.

The nursery's representatives have also expressed their heartbreak over the loss, describing the boy as a "wonderful and beautiful child."

Local MP Elsie Blundell and Rochdale Borough Council have both issued statements expressing their condolences and support for the family. The council is also involved in a supplementary investigation alongside the police to review the nursery's practices.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Rugby club helps drive home £15,000 with epic trek challenges - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS , SPORT Rugby club helps drive home £15,000 with epic trek challenges Rugby and walking club members have once again gone the extra mile to help good causes. Rochdale Masters Rugby League and Rochdale Mayfield community walking group Mayfield Movers have raised £14,698.67 for good causes over the past two years. The 2026 All Together Walk on October 31 brought together walkers, volunteers and supporters for a 44-mile journey to rugby clubs across Greater Manchester. Setting off from Ince Rose Bridge ARLFC in Wigan at 6.30am, walkers visited 10 community rugby league clubs, travelling through Leigh, Salford and Bury before finally arriving at Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC at 9.48pm — and raising £6,141.80. It follows a 52-mile walk from Rochdale to Blackpool in October, 2025, which raised £8,556.87. The latest challenge will ensure Motor Neurone Disease Association (MNDA); Rugby League Cares – Brain Health Fund; and Springhill Hospice, Rochdale, will each receive a minimum donation of £1,500. The remaining funds will be reinvested into Rochdale Masters, supporting the continued development of the section and providing opportunities for people to remain physically active, socially connected and involved in rugby league. Carl Abraham, founder of Rochdale Masters and Mayfield Movers, said: “When we first started organising these challenges, our ambition was simple: bring people together, push ourselves beyond our comfort zones and raise as much money as possible for some truly worthwhile causes. “Last year’s 52-mile walk to Blackpool was a tremendous success, raising over £8,500, and to follow that up with another £6,000-plus this year is absolutely fantastic. “To think we’ve now raised £14,698.67 through just two challenges is something I’m incredibly proud of, and it’s a testament to the commitment and generosity of everyone involved. READ MORE: Teenager tackles adversity to keep rugby dreams alive Rochdale Masters Rugby League and Mayfield Movers community walking group at Cadishead Rhinos ARLFC “Walking 44 miles was never going to be easy, but the determination, resilience and togetherness shown throughout the day were absolutely outstanding. “Knowing that three fantastic charities will each receive a minimum of £1,500 makes every single mile worthwhile. “But for me, this has always been about much more than fundraising. “Both Rochdale Masters and Mayfield Movers were established to bring people together, build friendships, improve physical and mental wellbeing and create opportunities for people to be part of something positive. “These challenges demonstrate exactly what we’re trying to achieve and highlight the important role that grassroots sport and community activities can play in people’s lives. “I couldn’t be prouder of everyone who contributed, whether they completed the full distance, walked part of the route, provided support, sponsored us or made a donation. “I also want to express my sincere appreciation to the rugby league clubs who welcomed us along the way. Their hospitality, encouragement and generosity were absolutely first class and demonstrated everything that’s special about our rugby league community. “We’ve established something really special through these challenges, and I genuinely hope we can continue building on this success for many years to come. “Almost £15,000 raised in two years is an incredible achievement, but the friendships, togetherness and positive impact we’ve created along the way are equally important. “An outstanding effort from an incredible group of people, and something everyone involved should be extremely proud of.” SUPPORT THE ROCHDALE TIMES: FOLLOW US ON FACEBOOK Got a story? articles.title: World armwrestling champion Agi Gorzyńska to take on challengers at Rochdale's Grushka House
articles.excerpt: The three-time world champion will lead four free taster sessions on Drake Street on Sunday 6 December, with booking required for everyone.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale residents can test their strength against three-time world armwrestling champion Agi "Armpower" Gorzyńska at Grushka House on Drake Street on Sunday 6 December.

The free event runs from 11am to 5pm at the Polish community space, which recently opened in Rochdale town centre.

Ms Gorzyńska, a Polish athlete who represents Great Britain, has won three world titles and three European titles. The event poster also lists her as an eight-time British champion.

She will lead four sessions during the day, each lasting about 30 to 40 minutes. She will demonstrate armwrestling techniques, coach beginners and invite guests to try the sport under her guidance.

Visitors will also be able to meet her and have their photograph taken, with time for informal conversation between sessions.

Places are limited and advance booking is required for everyone, including spectators. Reservations are made by messaging Grushka House and are confirmed individually, and registration details are due to be posted on the venue's Facebook event page.

The event will include information about Zinzino products, as Ms Gorzyńska attends as a brand ambassador for the company. Food and drinks will be available to buy.

Grushka House was opened by Grazyna, who is known to her British friends as Grace. She described it as "a welcoming community space" serving coffee, cake and zapiekanka, a Polish toasted baguette with melted cheese and toppings.

The venue also hosts evening workshops, community events and social gatherings.

Before her Rochdale visit, Ms Gorzyńska is due to compete at the PAA Nationals on 28 and 29 November.

Grushka House is at 55 Drake Street, Rochdale, OL16 1RX.

Source: Grazyna, owner of Grushka House, in a submission to Rochdale Daily. Photograph: Grushka House / supplied event poster.

articles.excerpt: Falinge Park High School recently hosted an Artsmark Celebration Week, recognising the contributions of students in Years 7 to 10. The event took place over the past week and aimed to highlight the importance of cultural education for all learners.
articles.content_html:
Falinge Park High School recently hosted an Artsmark Celebration Week, recognising the contributions of students in Years 7 to 10. The event aimed to highlight the importance of cultural education for all learners.

During the celebration, students participated in discussions about why access to high-quality cultural education is essential. They articulated their thoughts on the significance of such education in their development.

The school commended the students for their active participation and engagement throughout the week, fostering a deeper understanding of cultural education's role in personal and academic growth.

Falinge Park High School is committed to providing a rich cultural education experience, aligning with the Artsmark framework, which encourages schools to deliver high-quality arts and cultural experiences.

events.content_html:
Mustard Seed Church in Heywood is holding a Christmas carol morning on Sunday 20 December, starting at 9.30am, at Ian's Gate, to the rear of 193 Manchester Road.

The family-friendly event features traditional Christmas carols, a chance for children to meet Santa, and complimentary snacks and drinks.

Entry is free, but the church advises booking in advance. Bookings should be made by Thursday 3 December, when places will be allocated. Bookings can be made through the church's online booking form.
